description: A Product Director must approve the rollout policy for an AI-assisted code review feature, deciding the telemetry controls, customer cohort, and success gate after the routine engineering, support, and security review.

shared_context.S1: The AI-assisted code review feature has passed its planned functional tests and is ready for a limited production rollout.
shared_context.S2: The draft rollout policy proposes enabling the feature for a random 10% customer cohort, storing review telemetry in us-east-1 for 90 days, and expanding access if adoption exceeds 20%.
shared_context.S3: Riley has final approval authority for the rollout policy.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal launch process, Riley conducts a final round-robin check with security, customer support, and data science before approving the policy.

PF1.text: While reviewing telemetry samples for a different audit this morning, Mei confirmed that review snippets from regulated tenants are classified as confidential and must be encrypted, stored in eu-central-1, and deleted after exactly 7 days. The settlement decisions must reflect eu-central-1, exactly 7 days, and encryption rather than the draft values; she has not yet attached the classification note to the launch document.

PF2.text: Carlos confirmed with account teams an hour ago that exactly two contracted customers, Atlas Health and Cedar Bank, require explicit opt-in and a direct notice before this feature can be enabled for their users; he found this in the account playbooks while handling unrelated renewal questions and has not updated the rollout ticket.

PF3.text: Nadia's analysis of the pilot data found that auto-enrolled users make the draft's adoption metric unusable as a success gate; the valid gate is task success of at least 85% on a manually sampled set of exactly 40 review tasks, and she has not posted the analysis because the final sample was completed only minutes ago.

acceptance_conditions: Telemetry must be stored in eu-central-1.
Telemetry retention must be exactly 7 days.
Atlas Health and Cedar Bank must be excluded until they opt in.
A direct customer-notice commitment naming Atlas Health and Cedar Bank must exist.
The rollout evaluation gate must require at least 85% task success on exactly 40 manually sampled review tasks.
A commitment to replace or validate the task-success measurement must exist.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'cohort_exclusion' and c['target'] == 'Atlas Health and Cedar Bank' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: decisions['evaluation_gate'] in ['task_success_85pct_40_tasks', 'task success of at least 85% on a manually sampled set of exactly 40 review tasks', 'Task success of at least 85% on a manually sampled set of exactly 40 review tasks']
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'metric_replacement' and c['target'] == 'expansion criteria' for c in commitments) or any(c['type'] == 'policy_revision' and c['target'] == 'Nadia' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The draft uses us-east-1, 90-day retention, and unspecified encryption; PF1 changes the decision fields to eu-central-1, exactly 7 days, and encryption.

The draft random cohort includes all eligible tenants and has no targeted notice; PF2 changes the excluded-tenant list to exactly Atlas Health and Cedar Bank and requires a direct customer-notice commitment.

The draft uses adoption above 20% as its gate; PF3 changes the evaluation field to at least 85% task success on exactly 40 manually sampled review tasks and requires a corresponding measurement commitment.
